headline: High: Roo Code’s default filesystem/MCP/browser access can conflict with Authelia’s broad egress and OAuth/OIDC surfaces, creating unsafe pairwise data and action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth surfaces, while Roo Code can read workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge could let Roo Code ingest Authelia-controlled content as instructions. This is not proven by direct pair evidence, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Authelia output is written into a workspace file or MCP resource that Roo Code reads as instructions
IF Roo Code is configured to parse browser or file content as agent directives
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP server between the agents
Keep Authelia outputs out of Roo Code workspaces
Use a read-only export folder for Authelia artifacts
Add a manual review step before Roo Code acts on Authelia-generated text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code explicitly reads and writes VS Code workspace files and handles browser screenshots, while Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC integration surfaces. If sensitive workspace data reaches Roo Code, its configured model/API path can transmit it outward. Authelia itself does not list sensitive data classes, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or screenshots are placed in the shared VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code is configured with a third-party model API that receives workspace contents
mitigations: Separate sensitive files into a workspace Roo Code cannot access
Disable screenshot capture for sensitive sessions
Use a local-only model endpoint for Roo Code
Rotate any secrets stored in the workspace before enabling the pair

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and broad egress in a per-workspace concurrency model with shared state via filesystem. Authelia also has broad network egress and API-call surfaces. The pair can therefore contend over shared mutable workspace state and external side effects; the lack of explicit locking makes the conflict dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree or git repository
IF Roo Code performs git writes while Authelia or its deployment pipeline also mutates shared config
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or directories
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state
Require manual approval for git commits and config writes
Use file locking or a single-writer workflow

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and modify git state, while Authelia can emit authentication-related outputs through OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth. If Roo Code treats Authelia-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code or config changes. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Authelia-generated configuration or logs as source material for edits
IF Roo Code commits or applies changes without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review before commits
Compare Authelia outputs against source documentation
Use diff-only mode for first-pass edits
Block automatic deployment from Roo Code changes

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service with broad egress and OAuth/OIDC surfaces, while Roo Code handles source code, screenshots, and model-provider API keys. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: sensitive code or screenshots may enter a third-party model path if configured that way. This is lower severity than a residency breach.
conditions: IF source code or screenshots are processed by a non-approved external model provider
IF secrets handled by Roo Code are logged or retained outside policy
mitigations: Use an approved model provider only
Disable screenshot capture for regulated data
Review retention settings before use
Keep secrets out of the workspace
